metadata.source: National Treasury Annual Public Debt Management Report (APDMR); Budget Policy Statement; Controller of Budget National Government Budget Implementation Review Report (NG-BIRR); CBK Statistical Bulletin.
metadata.description: Kenya national fiscal summary — budget, revenue, borrowing, total debt service, and debt ceiling. Debt service follows the Treasury APDMR definition: interest payments PLUS principal redemptions (domestic + external). This matches the Treasury's own headline 'debt service to revenue' ratio.
metadata.notes: Fiscal summary baselines. REVENUE IS NOT STORED HERE: FY23/24 onward are derived on every run from Treasury's Budget Summary (Table 2, Ordinary Revenue = tax + non-tax excluding A-i-A and grants) by revenue_estimates.py, and appropriated_budget is derived from the Programme Based Budget book by budget_estimates.py. FY22/23 predates the fiscal-framework table in the current Budget Summary and is the one revenue figure still stored — see its total_revenue_stored_reason. Debt service follows the Treasury APDMR definition: interest payments PLUS principal redemptions.

FY 2023/24.title: Annual Public Debt Management Report 2023/2024
FY 2023/24.note: Headline ratio: total debt service KSh 1,640.1B / revenue KSh 2,406B = 68.3%.

FY 2025/26.title: 2025 Budget Policy Statement
FY 2025/26.note: Budgeted, not actual. Uses a FY25/26 budget estimate of TOTAL debt service (interest + principal redemptions) over tax + non-tax revenue so the published ratio stays comparable with the APDMR series while the 2025/26 APDMR is still pending. Will be revised once FY25/26 APDMR lands in Nov 2026.

methodology_notes.FY 2022/23 / 2023/24 / 2024/25: APDMR framing: total debt service (interest + principal redemptions) divided by tax+non-tax revenue including ministerial A-i-A.
methodology_notes.FY 2025/26: Budget estimate framed to stay comparable with the APDMR series: total debt service (interest + principal redemptions) divided by tax+non-tax revenue. Values are budgeted from the BPS until the FY2025/26 APDMR publishes.

definitions.debt_service_cost: FY22/23–FY24/25: TOTAL debt service per APDMR (interest + principal redemptions, domestic + external). FY25/26: budgeted total debt service using the same broad definition until the APDMR actual is published.
definitions.debt_service_per_shilling: Shillings of total debt service paid per KSh 100 of revenue. The ratio is derived from debt_service_cost / total_revenue at seed time.
definitions.total_revenue: FY22/23–FY24/25: tax + non-tax revenue including ministerial A-i-A (APDMR denominator). FY25/26: budgeted tax + non-tax revenue to preserve series comparability until the APDMR actual publishes.
definitions.appropriated_budget: COB original gross budget (National Government): gross ministerial recurrent + gross ministerial development + Consolidated Fund Services. Excludes the county equitable share. See budget_basis_source on each row for the document, page and quoted sentence.
definitions.recurrent_spending / development_spendin: NOT on the cob_gross basis. These remain the Budget Policy Statement / APDMR series they have always been, and were deliberately left unchanged when appropriated_budget moved to cob_gross on 2026-08-29 so that a budget-basis decision did not silently move four other published series. COB publishes its own composition for each year (quoted in budget_basis_source.composition where available); moving these fields onto it is a separate, deliberate change.

metadata.canonical_budget_basis_note: appropriated_budget is the Controller of Budget's ORIGINAL GROSS BUDGET for the National Government: gross ministerial (recurrent + development) expenditure PLUS Consolidated Fund Services. It EXCLUDES the county equitable share, which COB reports separately. This basis was chosen deliberately on 2026-08-29 over the Budget Policy Statement figures the file previously carried; every row now declares which basis its budget is on in budget_basis, and a live overlay may only replace a value that declares the SAME basis.
metadata.debt_ceiling_note: debt_ceiling and debt_ceiling_usage_pct are NULL on every row and must stay that way. The KES 10 trillion numerical ceiling they measured against was repealed by the PFM (Amendment) Act 2023 and replaced with a debt anchor of 55% of GDP in PRESENT-VALUE terms. Publishing 'debt ceiling usage 125%' is a ratio against an instrument that no longer exists — and this site's own homepage says the ceiling was repealed. If a ceiling ratio is wanted again it has to be computed against the PV anchor, which needs a PV-of-debt series we do not hold.
metadata.actual_debt_note: actual_debt is NULL on every row. It held 9,100 / 10,200 / 11,490 / 12,500 (KES billion) — the pre-correction debt series that DATA_CORRECTIONS_2026-08-29 replaced in debt_timeline with the CBK Statistical Bulletin values 9,146 / 11,140 / 10,925 / 12,299. Keeping both meant the API served two 'Kenya total debt by year' series differing by up to 939B. debt_timeline is the canonical one: it is CBK-sourced and every row must satisfy domestic + external = total. Read total debt from there.

budget_basis_source.title: National Government Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2022/23
budget_basis_source.publisher: Office of the Controller of Budget
budget_basis_source.quote: The approved gross budget for both National and County Governments for the FY 2022/23 amounted to Kshs.4.19 trillion ... and Kshs.515.18 billion cumulative County Governments Budget
budget_basis_source.derivation: COB states the FY2022/23 original gross budget only for National + County combined (4.19T). The National-Government figure is 4.19T less the 515.18B county budget stated in the same sentence = 3,674.8B, rounded to 3,675B. Cross-checked against the components COB lists on the same page (715.35B development + 2.97T recurrent = 3,685.4B, 0.3% apart — COB's own rounding).
budget_basis_source.composition: development 715.35B; recurrent 2.97T (MDA recurrent 1.40T + CFS 1.57T); county budget 515.18B (excluded)

fiscal_years.total_revenue_stored_reason: The Budget Summary's Table 2 and the 2026 BPS Annex Table 2 both start at FY 2023/24, so no document currently in the pipeline carries FY 2022/23 revenue. This 2,042 is APDMR ordinary revenue. It is the last stored revenue figure in this file; deriving it needs an older Budget Summary (the listing page still carries FY2022/23 and FY2023/24 editions) to be discovered by fiscal year rather than by recency.

budget_basis_source.title: National Government Budget Implementation Review Report FY 2023/24
budget_basis_source.publisher: Office of the Controller of Budget
budget_basis_source.quote: The National Government's original gross budget for FY 2023/24 amounted to Kshs.4.34 trillion, revised to Kshs.4.54 trillion in Supplementary Estimates I and Kshs.4.43 trillion in Supplementary Estimates II

fiscal_years.total_revenue_absent_reason: Derived live, not stored. seeding/domains/fiscal_summary/revenue_estimates.py discovers and parses the Treasury Budget Summary's Table 2 on every run and overlays the whole ordinary-revenue series onto these rows, gating each year on a column identity (ordinary + A-i-A == total), a cross-document check against the Budget Policy Statement, and a plausibility band. A year that fails is quarantined individually. Storing the figure here would freeze a number that Treasury republishes and revises annually.

debt_service_source.title: Programme Based Budget FY 2026/27 (Approved)
debt_service_source.note: Interest & redemption, the APDMR debt-service definition used by every other year in this file. Reconciles inside CFS 2,563.0B. Repeated here because the seeder's writer overwrites every column unconditionally, so omitting it would null the value the PBB overlay already established.

fiscal_years.appropriated_budget_absent_reason: This row exists to carry the FY2026/27 REVENUE estimate. The gross budget for the year is read live from the Programme Based Budget book by seeding/domains/fiscal_summary/budget_estimates.py, which gates it on three reconciliation identities and overlays it (with its own page-and-quote provenance) onto this row at seed time. Duplicating that figure here would create a second copy that can go stale against the book.
